name: Every Corner Deletion of a Peripheral Maximum Class Has a Peripheral Parent
statement: Let $M$ be a recursively peripheral maximum class of positive rank $r$ and $v$ any corner. Then $M\setminus\{v\}$ is recursively peripheral and has a recursively peripheral rank-$r$ maximum parent $N$ on one auxiliary coordinate $a$, with $\pi_XN=M$ and $N[a=0]=M\setminus\{v\}$. Thus the deletion belongs to $\mathcal P_0\cap\mathcal M_1$; for proper $M$, rank $r$ and one auxiliary are optimal.
proof: Order the corner support so the compatible face-avoiding predecessor respects a nested peripheral split of $M$. If the split coordinate is outside the corner support, apply induction in the large shore and monotonicity in the small shore. If it belongs to the support, the corner lies in the smaller shore; put that coordinate first and apply induction there. The resulting shores stay nested and peripheral. The standard one-corner parent supplies the required projection and section; nonmaximumity of a proper deletion proves optimality.
